## Decisions

- **Live stages are Frame Job's own DSP; Apple's units render offline (AU-3, S1).** S1's rule, fixed before its runs: a live stage allocates and locks nothing on the tap's thread, reads byte-identically twice and at any buffer size, sits within 0.1 dB of its analytic response, has one constant latency ≤ 512 samples, and eight stereo stages cost ≤ 1 % of real time. Frame Job's own stages passed all five; no Apple unit passed for any stage: their output depends on how the stream is cut into render calls (up to −34 dBFS for `AUDynamicsProcessor` on irregular slices, which the tap's cuts and the player's 4,096-frame buffers make), `AUPeakLimiter` limits sample peak at a fixed 0 dBFS (+3.10 dBTP on a crest signal), and `AUNBandEQ` was only 1.5–1
- **One fixed chain, each stage off and inert by default (AU-3, AU-54, AU-143, AU-66 (a)).** The clip's chain is isolation → voice effect → channels → high-pass/EQ → hum → noise reduction → gate → leveller → de-esser → compressor → limiter → fader; then the track's volume and pan, the track's compressor and limiter on its sub-mix (AU-151), and the export's master (AU-27). Isolation moved ahead of the live chain because it renders offline from the media (S2), and the voice effect renders from isolation's crossfade. A project using none of the clip and track stages plays as before and writes no new key (each is written only when set); its export now always passes the master, which leaves a mix under the ceiling sample-identical (AP2b's X6). (
- **Loudness is the export's figure, from a 10 ms cache (AU-10…AU-17, S4).** 100 ms blocks missed the export's own meter by up to −0.139 LU over random windows; 10 ms blocks stayed within 0.076 (97.5 % of 200 windows within 0.1 LU), and 10 ms is the peaks grid, so the waveform's window, the reversed mirror and the source map apply unchanged. The export copies a mono clip into both channels (+3.01 LU), so every reading counts mono twice: the owner's recording is −41.67 LUFS where its file reads −44.7. AU-4's gated target stands; speech-only loudness read 1.1–1.7 LU higher. (orig AP0 "S4", AP1)
- **The clip limiter is told the base volume and leads its own delay (AU-20…AU-26).** The fader is downstream of the tap, so the stage is told the clip's base volume, fades and ducks only ever lowering it (AU-22). It runs for the whole composition track once any clip asks, so the track's delay never changes at a cut (158 samples, led out by 1,975 ticks). Its detector takes the maximum over a 64-tap Kaiser (β 10) detector's phases and BS.1770 Annex 2's: a detector the size of Annex 2's alone let broadband onsets through by up to +0.97 dB, and Annex 2 over-reads speech by 0.14 dB, so a limiter exact by an accurate meter alone would read −0.86 dBTP on the export's meter. Two departures from S1's code, neither from its arithmetic: the FIR taps 
- **The export always runs a float master (AU-27…AU-29, #86).** S3 found two clips, each under its own limiter, reaching +1.49 dBTP through a crossfade, so a master limiter at `peak_dbtp` (−1 dBTP by default) runs on every export with sound, with no off switch; the loudness target now limits instead of capping, the gain solved through the limiter's model over 10 ms steps and capped at +40 dB. The mix is decoded as float (#86 closed) and written at 16 or 24 bits on WAV and AIFF, rounded once, never dithered. (orig AP2b)
- **Isolation is Apple's voice model, rendered offline and crossfaded (AU-50…AU-57, S2).** `AUSoundIsolation` with parameter 1 = 0 selects High Quality Voice (the unit's default, Voice, loses everything above 10.5 kHz). Each channel renders as its own mono render, the constant 4,440-frame latency pinned and discarded, 4 s of the media fed first. The unit's 50 % equals a sample-aligned 50/50 mix of dry and a 100 % render, so Amount is a crossfade of one cached render and is not in the cache key. Mid-file windows differ by about −51 dB from a whole-file render, so proofs compare levels and alignment, never bytes. De-reverb (survey B4) rides on it: C50 +5.2 dB and the late tail −5.3 dB on a synthetic RT60 0.6 s room, so the section says it "re
- **EQ is RBJ biquads in Double at 17 fixed positions (AU-30…AU-39).** Seven named slots and three presets, each preset writing only its own slot. The hum comb's Q is 10·k / A (A = 10^(−depth/40)): the plain Q = 10·k comb missed −depth once cascaded and cut the voice between harmonics, the adversary's objection, taken before the code. (orig AP3)
- **The gate's threshold is relative to the clip's loudness; the de-esser never boosts (AU-40…AU-49).** A level fixed in dBFS was what failed on this microphone (survey §2), so the gate reads the clip's own measured L, and an export waits for it. The draft de-esser `x − (1 − g)·band` boosted the sibilant band (+2.6 dB at 6 kHz for a 6 dB range, a 4th-order high-pass being 180° out at its cut), so the reduction goes through an LR4 crossover, `low + g·band`, and the Butterworth stays the sidechain only. (orig AP4)
- **Enhance Voice is a composite that writes ordinary settings, its volume solved on the processed sound (AU-60…AU-65).** It measures the clip and writes high-pass, isolation or noise reduction, gate, de-esser when the high band is hot, a compressor set from the clip's own level, the limiter and the volume, as one undo step; a second press changes nothing. The first attempt solved the volume through the compressor's block-rate model and exported the owner's recording at −13.95 LUFS for a −16 target: cleaning the pauses changes which blocks BS.1770's relative gate counts (the gate moved the export +2.4 LU, isolation +2.6 LU, the EQ −0.7 LU). On 2026-10-31 the owner chose (A), measure the processed sound, for Enhance and Loudness Normalize al
- **The leveller is a curve made ahead of time, applied with no state (AU-66, AU-67).** The first build, a slow stateful rider, could not meet its own acceptance row: its hold carried each segment's gain through a pause into the next, which started 12 dB off, so the off-mic fixture's range went 13.63 LU in, 13.96 out. On 2026-10-31 the owner chose look ahead: a gain curve per phrase from the clip's loudness and speech, so each phrase starts at its level (13.63 → 2.32 LU), and the per-phrase start held to ±3 dB (the owner's choice on the same measurement; the material's sentences open louder than their middles). ## Decisions

- **The writer is `AVAssetWriter` fed by a data output, not the movie output (CAM-2, CR0).** At 1552 × 1552 (W2) and 1920 × 1080 (W1) alike the movie output wrote 93.2 % of span × rate with 12 gaps per file at 27.94 fps and took 1008–1044 ms to start or resume; the writer (W3) wrote 99.9 % with no gap, started in 10–14 ms and resumed in 5–26 ms (P2). On macOS a session keeps a requested format only while the device's configura
- **The best format is the largest LANDSCAPE area (CAM-3).** CAM-2's rule picked the built-in camera's square 1552 × 1552, so CAM-3 applies it to the formats wider than tall: 1760 × 1328 @ 30 on the FaceTime HD Camera, 1920 × 1440 @ 60 on the iPhone, 1920 × 1080 @ 60 on OBS Virtual Camera. Step 2 measured the writer there first: W3 0.9993 in every run, P2's median resume 15.16 ms. (orig CR1a)
- **A camera recording starts on a warm stream (CAM-3's warm-up).** A cold camera's first intervals ran 33.3, 33.3, then five at 43.3 ms, which left segment 0 at 0.975 of span × rate in every run while a resumed segment read 0.999. So segment 0's writer is armed only after five consecutive intervals within 15 % of the frame duration, bounded at 1 s, with `camera.note` past the bound (G6: a hold of about 0.53 s, 13 buffers). Th
- **The entitlement is added though the spike found it not needed (CAM-3).** CR0's T2, a hardened binary without `com.apple.security.device.camera`, delivered frames, but under the terminal's grant; road map 3 found the signed app needed the microphone's entitlement where a bare probe did not, so the camera follows that finding, and `NSCameraUsageDescription` and the dist checks' exact sets carry it. No Continuity key: CR0's D
- **The microphone is placed by `startPTS` on the host clock (CAM-3).** The two offsets, by `startPTS` and by callbacks, differ by about 63 ms with the writer (P2) and by 210–241 ms with the movie output. Only a person's clap (REC-12) measures the truth. The tool's `mic_offset` read −59.9 to −80.1 ms across the Release runs. The screen recorder's own microphone, placed by callbacks, is #370. (orig CR0, CR1b–CR2c)
- **One shared session queue fixes #373 (CAM-7).** A fresh capture built in the same main turn as the stop of another capture of its device recorded no frame (CR1c's `prepare-ignored`; CR2b's `session-queue-per-capture` mutant reproduced it: fresh starts at 1.035 and 1.037 s, "The camera delivered no frame."). Every capture's lock, format, `startRunning` and `stopRunning` now run on one serial queue, and `stop(completion:)` an
- **The screen's start is E2, and the frame watch comes off the stream for a resume (CAM-9).** CR0's re-run on the final instrument found E1 (the did-start's arrival) past the 16.7 ms bound in 4 of 8 runs (−19.9 to −21.0 ms) while E2, the first complete `.screen` frame at or after it, read +0.49 ms in all 16. CR3a first left the watch on through a resume: every resumed segment's `SCRecordingOutput` failed "to process first sam
- **The camera begins before the screen, so the head trim is the usual path (CAM-10).** Started in one run-loop turn, the writer's camera began 87–130 ms before the screen file in CR0, and every `cameraOffset` in CR3a's G16 was negative (−0.032 to −0.146 s). So each camera clip is asked at its screen clip's start plus its offset, floored there and at the previous camera clip's end, and head-trimmed by the microphone's shared d
- **The corner is fixed (CAM-10 (3)).** A box a quarter of the canvas wide and a third tall, inside the 90 % ring of View ▸ Safe Areas, by one `set_video {x, y, scale}`, and the clip stays an ordinary clip to move. L5 read 1760 × 1328 → (625, 306, 0.27108) on a 1920 × 1080 canvas. The ring is named by its percentage because spec §4.1 calls the 90 % ring title-safe. (orig CR3b)
- **The box is a control of its own (CAM-11).** "Record the camera too" under Include Frame Job windows, live only with a display or the Window row, persisted in `FrameJobRecordingCameraBeside`. An "Off" row in the Camera popup was not chosen: it would change what the shared camera key means for Source Camera and for hot-plug. The press reads Screen Recording, then Camera, then Microphone. (orig CR3c)
- **Hot-plug never writes a key (CAM-8).** The popups follow the devices while the panel is up and idle, a list compared before it is rebuilt, a returning camera chosen again with its format; a change made during a recording waits for idle. (orig CR2c)

## Known limits

- **One rate per format** (CAM-6): a camera records at a format's highest frame rate; a lower rate within the format's range is not offered.
- **The corner is fixed** (CAM-10 (3)): the bottom-right corner, a quarter wide and a third tall inside the 90 % ring, with no control for another corner, scale or inset; the clip is moved by hand afterwards.
- **A left-out segment's camera is kept, never landed** (CAM-10 (2)): its screen movie would not read, so its camera file stays on disk, named in `kept_files` and the note, and only its microphone takes the slot.
- **The watch's remove is at the resume, not the pause** (CAM-9 (6)): a remove at the pause was not measured, and the pause leaves the watch on the stream as measured. One run in which only the re-add was kept, without the remove, also passed. The re-add's throw is structural only: on a never-starte
- **The camera offset's spread**: the Release tool runs read −161.5 and −170.4 ms, past CR3a's 32–146 ms and within G16's 0.5 s bound, one run each.
- **A tool start pays the warm-up** (CAM-7 (7)): it never adopts the panel's prepared capture, so it builds its own (about 0.77 s in G12 and G14), and the panel's preview reads "The camera is recording." meanwhile.
- **The microphone's truth is a person's**: the offset by `startPTS` and the offset by callbacks differ by about 63 ms with the writer; REC-12's clap is the measurement.
- **A virtual camera**: OBS Virtual Camera delivered frames with OBS running (X1); without its host app it is not measured. No spike row recorded from the iPhone; its pairing is REC-16.
- **Synthetic and host fixtures only**: the granted tiers run on this Mac's cameras under the terminal's grants and skip by name without them; the look, framing and lining up are REC-12..REC-18.

- **AV1's rate is a soft cap, quality first (CX-13; the owner chose option 2, 2026-10-28).** Single-pass VBR (CX-9) undershot a real clip to 0.667–0.670 of its target. /// The sixteen kinds, in E8's order — the core's `VoiceKind`, spelled as it
/// persists them.
enum VoiceKind: String, Codable, CaseIterable {
    case pitch, high, deep, robot, bass, treble, bright, telephone, radio, lofi, distorted, echo,
        room, hall, plate, cathedral

    var group: VoiceGroup {
        switch self {
        case .pitch, .high, .deep, .robot: return .voice
        case .bass, .treble, .bright, .telephone, .radio: return .tone
        case .lofi, .distorted: return .character
        case .echo, .room, .hall, .plate, .cathedral: return .space
        }
    }

    /// "Voice: Pitch" … "Space: Cathedral" (AU-146).
    var title: String {
        let name: String
        switch self {
        case .pitch: name = "Pitch"
        case .high: name = "High"
        case .deep: name = "Deep"
        case .robot: name = "Robot"
        case .bass: name = "Bass"
        case .treble: name = "Treble"
        case .bright: name = "Bright"
        case .telephone: name = "Telephone"
        case .radio: name = "Radio"
        case .lofi: name = "Lo-Fi"
        case .distorted: name = "Distorted"
        case .echo: name = "Echo"
        case .room: name = "Room"
        case .hall: name = "Hall"
        case .plate: name = "Plate"
        case .cathedral: name = "Cathedral"
        }
        return "\(group.title): \(name)"
    }

### Phase 0–1: groundwork and cutting moves
- **`model.rs` holds only type declarations.** Lookups and `validate` went to `model_query.rs`,
  and the serde defaults stayed in `model.rs`, because an absent key's meaning is schema (orig
  §2 P0).
- **Counts live in one place.** The README no longer counts tools; `rc_op_names` and the parity
  check are the authority.
- **The six placement ops are core ops, and none goes in `edit_clip.rs`.** They are `slip`,
  `roll` (`edit_edge.rs`), `lift_range`, `close_gap` (`edit_time.rs`), `insert_clip` and
  `overwrite_clip` (`edit_insert.rs`). Insert and overwrite are single ops so that each is one
  undo step and one tool.
- **Locks.** `close_gap` and `insert_clip` refuse on a locked track, and `overwrite_clip` does
  not, because a lock only governs what may shift. `close_gap` checks overlap per touched track
  only, and it closes fully or not at all.
- **A source window's head, window and remaining length have one home.** That home is now
  `source_window.rs` (D4). A clamp BOUND snaps directionally (`time.rs`
  `snap_up_to_frame`/`snap_down_to_frame`), never to the nearest frame. `whole_media_length`
  returns a SNAPPED length: an unsnapped 5 s still made every overwrite on a /1001 timeline a
  silent no-op.
- **`lift_range` and `ripple_delete_range` share the same two helpers and differ only in the
  shift.** The helpers are `ordered_range` and `clear_range`.
- **The media selection is document view state.** `ProjectDocument.selectedMedia` is the fourth
  piece of view state and is clamped like the rest. `ProjectDocument.targetTrack` is the one
  rule for "which track does a command without a track act on".
- **A modifier-less menu key equivalent must be guarded against text editing.** AppKit resolves
  it ahead of the first responder. The same reasoning is why most later commands take no key.
### Phase 2: clip identity (v3)
- **`set_clip` takes a patch** (`{name?, label?}`: absent keeps, `null` clears), and an empty or
  blank string clears too. The name fallback lives in exactly one place,
  `ProjectSnapshot.name(of:)`.
- **The label is a badge and never a tint.** The kind owns the tint.
- **`paste_attributes` replaces each group WHOLE and never merges.** A text clip keeps its
  `content`; a shape keeps `kind`, size, `from` and `to`. Speed, `enabled`, actions, the
  transition, the source, the name and the label do not travel. A named group missing on either
  side is an `Err`, all or nothing. The source is the payload's EARLIEST clip, not the first in
  the array, and each copied group is re-checked with `check_group`.
- **Solo is a mixer switch on the set, and mute wins.** The rule is
  `silenced = muted || (any solo && !solo)` (`audio.rs`). It is judged per container and acts
  only as an envelope. "Solo A" gives a plan string byte-identical to "mute everything but A".
- **The inline rename editor drops unchanged and empty commits, and its field follows its
  target.** A `relocate` closure moves the field on every relayout instead of ending it.
### Phase 3: silences, zoom, obscure (v4)
- **Silences are cut by `ripple_delete_ranges` in one op; the singular form delegates to the
  plural.** A span is silent only where EVERY voice in scope is quiet, and a voice the mix
  silences (muted or soloed out) is dropped from the scope. A nest is a WALL: its sound counts,
  but no cut may intersect it. `detect_silence` runs on main, does not clamp its numbers to the
  sheet's ranges, and echoes them back. Road map 4 later replaced the level test with Silero VAD.
- **`add_zoom_action` is a core op, because the placement maths belongs to the core
  (`edit_zoom.rs`).** It reads rotation and crop evaluated at `at`; a null region zooms BACK to
  the stored base `scale`/`x`/`y`; the scale is clamped before the offsets follow it; and the end
  patch's keys are exactly `scale`, `x` and `y`. Its `curve` argument defaults to easing both
  ends, because adding it later would have split one gesture into two ops.
- **One region frame.** `model_regions.rs` defines one coordinate frame (the centre in source
  pixels, measured from the cropped rect's centre) and one `SpotShape`. A later region joins
  them.
- **The list-interpolation rule applies to LIST ENTRIES only (`actions.rs`,
  `ENTRY_DISCRIMINANTS`).** A list interpolates per index when the lengths match and each
  entry's discrete fields agree; otherwise it switches at the end. Named objects such as the
  spotlight keep the old rule.
- **Obscure runs between the sharpen and the point filters.** Running after the sharpen stops
  the unsharp term from putting detail back. Running before the filters makes the region graded
  like the picture around it.
- **Overlapping regions apply the stronger hiding alone.** Strength is measured as a length in
  source pixels × mix, and a tie goes to pixelate. The cover is weighted by each slot's own
  strength, so adding a region can never un-hide.
- **Defaults hide.** A region defaults to pixelate at amount 1 with feather 20, and a NaN amount
  clamps to 1. A list write whose LENGTH differs lands on BASE props.
- **Canvas modes are overlays whose presence is the mode.** `armCanvasMode` ends every other
  armed mode.
### Phase 4: words (v5)
- **The recipe computes the reveal.** The text layer carries `reveal`, `reveal_phase` and
  `reveal_kind` (by name), always emitted. `animation` is STRIPPED from the description, so an
  unanimated hash is unchanged (`recipe_text.rs` `Reveal`).
- **`reveal_phase` is the DRAW ORDER, and a tent keeps its first phase for life.** A tent is the
  case `in + out > duration`. The phase may turn only where the reveal is 1.
- **`text.animation` has three keys and no curve.** Overlapping phases degrade to the minimum of
  the two ramps rather than refusing, and both halves are measured on the clip's own duration.
  The layout cache key excludes the reveal, so the reveal cannot reflow the text.
- **The cue rules live in `CaptionCues` and apply only to producers that invent line breaks.**
  The rules are ≤2 lines, ≤42 characters, ≤6 s, and a gap of at least one frame. The SRT
  importer never applied them. `CaptionLayout` is the one place any producer lays out captions.
- **`transcribe` refuses a missing grant; only the sheet asks for it.** The caller's own mistakes
  are answered first, then an unknown language, then the grant, then a missing model. A job's
  failure is reported per job, and a clip with its audio switched off is skipped.
- **A partially revealed outlined line is drawn inside a transparency layer.** Otherwise the
  fill and the stroke fade separately.
- **Caption times round-trip at every rate.** Byte identity with a foreign file needs a
  whole-millisecond frame.
- **The inspector pane's bottom pin sits at priority 249, one below the sections' 250.** A tie
  made renders bistable across processes. Recognise that symptom by identical input scoring
  differently across runs.
- **A section exists only once `ClipPane.makeSections()` calls it.**
- **#36: the canvas text editor is sized from `LayerRenderers.measuredSize`, the same
  measurement that sizes the applied box.**
- **#37: K-2.** Apply goes through `performGroupedEdit`.
### Phase 5: sound (no schema change)
- **The meter reads the existing PreEffects tap and multiplies by the plan's envelope.** A
  second PostEffects tap cannot exist: an input has one `audioTapProcessor`, and the tap takes
  one flag or the other. Moving the DSP tap would reorder the channel strip. The number is exact
  per track but is a SUM of tracks, not a device measurement.
- **Metering happens only in the playback build** (`metering: true` from
  `Playback.startRebuild`), and that build taps every track. Export and `render_frame` are
  untouched.
- **`LevelMeter` publishes raw values; the view owns the ballistics.** It uses the app's only
  `import Synchronization`: relaxed atomics, because the render thread may neither lock nor
  allocate.
- **The mono fold goes after the compressor and before the pan.** After a pan it would
  self-cancel. It averages every channel.
- **Normalise REPLACES `volume`, writes BASE props and works per clip.** Replacing makes it
  idempotent. The source window comes from the PLAN segment, which refuses every case with no
  audio. The 4× clamp is reported where it applies, and failures come back under `skipped`.
- **Loudness is measured on EVERY export that has sound.** That costs about 0.1× the wall time
  of a picture export and 0.5× of an audio-only one.
  - The measurement uses its own composition, reads float and uses the BS.1770-4 gates.
  - The gain is gain only, with no limiter.
  - A bare `peak_dbtp` is refused.
- **WAV and AIFF are 16-bit only.** Their LPCM rows carry a non-null `avf_preset`, which now
  means only "AVFoundation writes this".
- **#34: R2-1.** One composition track per source stream description.
### Phase 6: looks (v6)
- **Blend is programmable blending through framebuffer fetch (`blendPremultiplied`).**

- Landing: `app/Sources/RecordingLanding.swift`, `+Placing`, `+Microphone`, and `ProjectDocument+Recording.swift` (`untitled(around:)`). `adoptImported` lives in `ProjectDocument.swift`.
- Chrome: `app/Sources/RecorderPanelController.swift` with `+Rows`, `+Recording`, `+Pause`, `+Landing` and `+Picker`; `RecorderStatusItem.swift`; `AppDelegate+Recording.swift`; the File menu item in `AppDelegate+Menus.swift`; the quit guard in `AppDelegate.swift`; the welcome button in `WelcomeWindo
- Tool: `app/Sources/AgentServer+Recording.swift`, `+RecordingArguments`, `+RecordingResult`, `+RecordingChrome` (the tool's status item, B27), and the catalog entry in `AgentCatalog+Files.swift` (the R1 toll cut from `AgentCatalog.swift`).
- Composition: `CompositionBuilder.heldTail` in `app/Sources/CompositionBuilder.swift`. The sparse-track tail is in `MediaImporter.swift`, and `MediaImporter+Probe.swift` came from R1's mid-wave toll.
- Build: `project.yml` (`entitlements`, `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription`). `app/FrameJob.entitlements` is generated and git-ignored.
- Proof: `tools/proof/recording_spike.py` (R0 q1–q7, re-runnable), `recording_probe.py` (a probe over all of `app/Sources`, with a faked session and its own granted tier), and `recording_proof.py` (MCP, headless plus granted tiers). `tools/proof/README.md` holds the terminal-grant launch note.
## Known limits
- **TCC attribution:** a shell-launched binary runs under the TERMINAL's grants (R0 q1). A proof's instance therefore never tests Frame Job.app's own grant. `open -a … --env … --args …` gives an instance responsible for itself. `open -a` activates an existing instance instead of launching a new one.
- **Host state is a proof input.** A locked console lists 0 shareable displays under a true preflight. A muted output reaches the tap unreliably. Another app's sound lands in the tap. A Bluetooth OUTPUT gives the system-audio tap digital silence. A Bluetooth INPUT makes the mic lag the picture (see 
- **A variable-rate recording in a new project gives an inexact canvas rate only via File ▸ Open**, not via the recorder. At such a rate, "touching" segments may have a sub-frame gap.
- **Stopping and pausing edge cases** (documented in `ScreenRecorder+Pause.swift`):
  - A pause within ~10 ms of a resume's add can close an unopened file. Since B17 that empty movie is left out and named, not the recording's failure.
  - A mic start then stop before its first sample gives −11805 with no file. Since B17 it is that segment's `micProblem` alone, not `microphoneProblem` for the whole session.
  - A mic writer poisoned by a device profile switch (AirPods on first use, `'pck?'` −11800) fails every later segment's mic file.
- **A label past 9:59:59 is wider than the status item's one length.** The item is sized for ten hours; a longer recording's title is wider than `itemLength` (unmeasured how the bar draws it).
- **The countdown's meter holds its last pre-roll level through the ~0.1–0.2 s of arming**: the recorder publishes nothing while `.arming`, and `ScreenRecorder.swift` (399) was not touched to meter there (B27).
- **`recordedDuration` on `SCRecordingOutput` is whole seconds.** It serves the timer only, never an offset.
- **Structural-only coverage:** four rules are read, not driven, by the probe — the tool's `try?` on a nil, `freeze()`, the quit guard's `openMenu()`, and the panel close in `.starting`.
- **Rejected or left out:** camera recording (a second capture stack; spec §1 non-goal); keystroke/click callouts (event tap plus Input Monitoring; only `showMouseClicks` is taken); a global stop hotkey (needs a grant); trimming the countdown or any post-processing; recording into the package; HDR (

A microphone is a SECOND file (<stem> (Microphone).m4a) landing as a second clip on a new back track named Microphone, at the picture's start minus mic_offset — the measured lead of one file over the other, in ticks, positive meaning the picture began after the microphone; a negative start is the head trimmed, not a clip placed late. 152 04.3e-inspector-transcript-tab.md
# 4.3e Inspector — the Transcript tab

The inspector's fifth tab, fourth in the strip between Document and Assistant (§4.3a; road map
"creator-jobs" TX2a, TX2b, TX3a and TX3b; §11 TX-20…TX-27, TX-30…TX-34). View ▸ Transcript ⌃⌘T
shows the inspector if it is hidden, picks the tab and makes its view first responder;
`select_inspector_tab {tab: "transcript"}` reaches it too. Its content is view
state, never saved; the edits it makes are Delete Words and Delete Pause (below).

**What it shows.** TX1's timeline transcript (§7.9f, §11 TX-10): every heard
word of the edited container — the open nest when one is open — in timeline
order, in paragraphs, each led by its timecode in the canvas's timecode style
(`ReelTime.format`). A paragraph breaks where the track or the speaker label
changes, where two clips (or nest paths) on one track leave 1.5 s or more
between their words, and inside one clip where the voice cache holds 1.5 s of
source time below the voice threshold between two words — with no voice cache,
where 1.5 s of source time lies between them (§11 TX-22). Words that cannot be
cut (§11 TX-11: inside a nest, under a transition, on a locked track) are
faint, and hovering one shows its sentence.

**The bar** (§11 TX-24) is pinned above the text and does not scroll with it:
the pane's one header, hosted by the inspector above its scroll view as the
Clip tab's header is. Two rows, each a label at the inspector's label width
and a popup spanning the rest: **Words from** and **Language**. Under them the
status row, its sentence wrapping, with **Stop** at its right while the tab
reads on this Mac, or **Read** once stopped. Then the wrapping notes: the
same-speech notes (from the words shown), then at most three "clip N —
reason" rows for clips with no words, then "…and N more clips with no
words.", whose tooltip lists the rest. What is empty collapses.

**Words from** (§11 TX-25) lists "All tracks", then each track of the edited
container by name, in the project's order; one choice. With a track chosen
the tab shows only the words on that track — its tokens and their ids are
exactly `get_timeline_transcript {tracks: [id]}`'s — and reads on this Mac
only the media with a clip on that track. A chosen track that leaves the
container falls back to All tracks. The clips with no words are listed for
every track, as the tool lists them.

**Language** (§11 TX-25) lists "Automatic (<the Mac's default>)" — its identifier, en-US —, then every
recognition language installed on this Mac, by name, read once each time the
tab is shown; with none installed it is dimmed. A choice drops the words read
on this Mac and reads them again in that language, each media's run kept
beside the others (`<media>-<language>.json`); a cloud transcript still wins
(TR-11). Both choices are the window's view state: kept while the window is
open, whether the tab shows or not, and never saved.

**Following the playhead.** The highlight is the latest word whose start is at
or before the playhead, an accent-tinted rect behind it, so a word stays lit
through the pause after it. While the transport plays, the view keeps it in
sight unless the person scrolled within the last 3 s.

**Seeking.** A click on a word moves the playhead to its frame-snapped start;

- **The launch lock is held until the poll ends, and sits beside the socket.** If the lock were released straight after `open`, a second proxy's re-check would find nothing answering yet and launch a second instance. Keeping `agent.launch.lock` beside the socket gives a proof's s
- **A session whose launch timed out is stranded.** It launches no other instance, and its later calls answer the timeout sentence. Each session's check and launch are one critical section, after the review found two concurrent calls could both launch. (MC-4; orig Record ▸ MC3 de
